claims.text: The starting CoCrFeNi alloy is a homogeneous matrix without intrinsic self-lubricating secondary phases.
A minor alloying addition can promote precipitation or in-situ formation of a self-lubricating phase in CoCrFeNi during service.
The alloying addition can produce the self-lubricating phase without significantly changing the bulk CoCrFeNi matrix composition.
The resulting self-lubricating phase will be nanoscale and may be an oxide or intermetallic precipitate.
The self-lubricating phase will segregate to the sliding interface.
Segregation of the phase will form a continuous, stable, high-temperature-resilient tribofilm.
The tribofilm will reduce direct metal-to-metal contact.
The tribofilm will compensate for temperature-induced lattice disorder in the matrix.
Increasing temperature increases lattice disorder and consequently friction in the starting CoCrFeNi alloy.
Wear rate in the starting CoCrFeNi alloy increases as temperature rises.
Rising temperature degrades the surface integrity of the starting CoCrFeNi alloy.
Relative to unmodified CoCrFeNi, the modified alloy will have significantly lower coefficient of friction throughout room temperature to 800 °C.
Relative to unmodified CoCrFeNi, the modified alloy will have a reduced wear rate throughout room temperature to 800 °C.
The friction and wear improvements will be especially pronounced near 800 °C.
The beneficial effect is expected under moderate loads and controlled, mildly oxidizing ambient conditions.
Extreme loads or highly corrosive environments may prevent formation or stability of the tribofilm and limit its effectiveness.
